\[
B(x, y) = \sum_{i + j \le d} a_{ij}\, x^i y^j,
\qquad
I'(p) = I(p) - \bigl(B(p) - \bar B\bigr)
\]

The formula shows the default parameter values.

where

- \(B\): The fitted background surface
- \(a_{ij}\): The coefficients of the surface
- \(d\): The degree
- \(\bar B\): The mean of the surface over the image

B is a polynomial surface of degree d, with x and y scaled to -1 to 1. Each RANSAC trial picks as many random grid samples as B has coefficients, and fits B to them by least squares. It then counts the inliers, the samples within the threshold of B. Fischler and Bolles keep the trial with the most inliers. scikit-image then fits B to all of its inliers. The corrected image I' subtracts B minus its mean from each channel, so the background becomes even and the mean brightness stays. Objects are outliers, so they do not bend the fit.
